ingredients.note: cognac, for the sauce; plus a dash for the flambe and at the end

ingredients.name: bacon
ingredients.note: smoked pork belly, bacon or pancetta, in cubes

ingredients.name: mushrooms
ingredients.note: button, or other forest mushrooms, quartered

ingredients.name: white bread
ingredients.note: cut into triangles for croutons, optional

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for frying the chicken and croutons, plus the beurre manie; amount not stated

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: mixed with an equal amount of butter for the beurre manie; amount not stated

steps.text: The day before, put the chicken pieces in a large bowl with the carrot, onion, shallot, garlic, bouquet garni, peppercorns, cognac, oil and red wine. Cover and chill for at least 6 hours, turning the chicken now and then.

Take the chicken out of the marinade and dry every piece thoroughly with kitchen towel, and dry the marinade vegetables separately. Strain the marinade into a saucepan and reduce it for 10-15 minutes, skimming off any scum. Warm and reduce the chicken stock in the same way.
Heat the oven to 200 C. Brown the chicken in a casserole with butter and oil over medium heat, skin side first, until golden, then set aside.
Cook the dried marinade vegetables in the same dish for a couple of minutes, return the chicken, then add a splash of cognac on high heat and flambe it.

Pour in the reduced marinade wine and reduce on medium heat for 10 minutes. Top up with the stock until it just covers the chicken and season lightly. Add the bouquet garni, cover and cook in the oven for 30 minutes.
While it cooks, simmer the pearl onions with butter, sugar and a little water under a parchment lid until the water evaporates and they are lightly caramelised. Set aside.
Fry the quartered mushrooms in foaming butter until golden and set aside. Fry the bacon cubes until lightly crisp, then return the mushrooms and mix. Fry the bread triangles in butter until golden.

Lift the chicken onto a tray and rest it. Strain the sauce through a sieve, discard the vegetables and return the sauce to the pan. Check the seasoning and thicken with a little beurre manie, equal parts butter and flour, until it coats a spoon.
Stir in the bacon and mushrooms and a dash of cognac, and bring to the boil. Serve the chicken in the sauce topped with the caramelised onions, croutons and parsley.

title: Beef bourguignon
description: Chuck beef marinated overnight in red wine, browned with bacon, mushrooms and pearl onions, then slow-cooked in the oven in a thickened wine and stock sauce.

ingredients.name: chuck steak
ingredients.note: chuck beef, cut in 4-5 cm cubes, marinated

ingredients.name: carrot
ingredients.note: large, about 300 g, cut on an angle into 4-5 cm pieces, marinated

ingredients.name: pearl onions
ingredients.note: or small round pickling onions, marinated

ingredients.name: red wine
ingredients.note: pinot noir or other red; marinade, then reduced by half

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: olive, canola or vegetable, for browning

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: 3/4 tsp on the beef plus 1/4 tsp in the stew, more to taste at the end

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: on the beef, plus pepper in the stew

ingredients.name: bacon
ingredients.note: one piece, cut into 1 cm batons

steps.text: Marinate the beef, carrots, pearl onions, bay leaf, thyme and red wine in a non-reactive dish or bag in the fridge overnight, at least 12 and up to 24 hours.

Strain the marinade into a bowl and separate the beef, carrots and onions. Boil the wine in a saucepan, skimming, until reduced by half, and set aside. Heat the oven to 160 C fan (180 C conventional).
Pat the beef dry and season with 3/4 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Brown it in 3 batches in 2 tbsp of the oil in a large oven-proof pot over high heat, adding more oil if needed, and remove to a bowl.

Fry the bacon for 3 minutes until golden and add to the beef. Cook the mushrooms for 5 minutes until golden and set aside, then cook the onions for 5 minutes until golden in patches and add to the mushrooms.
Melt the butter, add the carrots and cook 3-4 minutes until golden in patches, then add the garlic for 1 minute. Stir in the tomato paste for 2 minutes, then the flour for 2 minutes.

Slowly stir in the beef stock so the flour dissolves without lumps, then add the reduced wine and mix until mostly smooth. Return the beef and bacon with the thyme, bay leaf, 1/4 tsp salt and pepper, and stir well.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook in the oven for 1 hour. Stir in the mushrooms and onions, cover and cook another 1 1/2 hours until the beef is fall-apart tender.
Taste the sauce and add salt if needed. For the best flavour leave the stew overnight and reheat gently. Serve sprinkled with parsley, over mashed potato if you like.

title: French Onion Soup
description: Slowly caramelised onions simmered in beef stock with white wine, thyme and bay, ladled into bowls and topped with cheesy baguette toast.

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: brown or yellow, peeled, halved and thinly sliced top to bottom

ingredients.name: beef stock
ingredients.note: good quality, low salt; chicken also works

ingredients.name: parsley
ingredients.note: fresh parsley or thyme leaves, to garnish

steps.text: Melt the butter in a heavy casserole over medium heat. When it foams, add the onions and stir to coat.
Cook on medium-low for 30 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the onions are soft and semi-transparent.
Add salt, turn the heat up to medium or medium-high and cook 20-30 minutes more, stirring more often, until deep golden and sweet.
Add the wine and simmer hard for 2 minutes, scraping up the bottom. Sprinkle over the flour and cook 1 minute.
Add the stock, thyme and bay leaves. Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Toast each side of the baguette slices under a high grill, top with cheese and grill until melted with brown spots.
Season the soup to taste, ladle into bowls and top with one or two cheesy toasts and a little parsley.

title: Tuna salad niçoise
description: A niçoise salad of canned tuna, lettuce, green beans, new potatoes, tomatoes, olives and boiled eggs, dressed with a lemon, Dijon and anchovy vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: medium, finely grated, for the vinaigrette

ingredients.name: tuna
ingredients.note: high-quality, packed in olive oil, drained

ingredients.name: lettuce
ingredients.note: head of leaf lettuce, ripped into large pieces

steps.text: Whisk the garlic, anchovy paste, lemon juice, Dijon, lemon zest, salt and pepper in a bowl. Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while whisking until the dressing is combined.
Boil the green beans for 1 minute, drain and chill in an ice-water bath. Dry them and set aside.
Boil the new potatoes until soft, about 15 minutes. Cool in cold water, pat dry and halve or quarter them.
Boil the eggs for about 8 minutes, cool in cold water, then peel and cut into quarters.
Spread the lettuce over a large platter and arrange the tuna, beans, potatoes, tomatoes, olives and red onion in groups on top. Tuck in the eggs.
Scatter the capers, black pepper and sea salt flakes over the top. Drizzle with some of the vinaigrette and serve at once with the rest on the side, plus warm baguette if you like.

title: Paella
description: Seafood paella with squid, prawns and mussels cooked in a sofrito of onion, pepper and tomato, with saffron fish broth, round rice and a crusty socarrat base.

ingredients.name: squid
ingredients.note: cleaned tube, cut into small squares

ingredients.name: passata
ingredients.note: tomato sauce (called tomato puree in the video); 1/2 cup

ingredients.name: smoked paprika
ingredients.note: sweet smoked Spanish paprika; a generous 1/2 tsp in the video

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: sea salt, to taste; for seasoning the oil and the sofrito

steps.text: Mince the garlic, dice the onion and pepper, and cut the squid into small squares. Have the prawns and cleaned mussels ready.
Heat the oil in a paella pan over medium-high heat, salt it, and cook the squid for 1.5-2 minutes. Remove it to a plate.
Cook the onion and garlic for 1 minute, then add the pepper and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce (passata), salt, pepper and smoked paprika and cook for 2 minutes until thickened. Return the squid.
Pour in the fish broth and saffron and bring to the boil. Scatter in the rice, stir once to spread it, and cook 5 minutes.
Add the prawns and mussels without stirring again, just shaking the pan, and cook 5 more minutes. Lower to low-medium heat and simmer about 10 minutes, until the broth is nearly absorbed.
For the socarrat, raise to medium-high for 1-2 minutes, then turn off the heat, cover and rest 5 minutes.
Uncover and garnish with parsley and lemon wedges.

title: Patatas bravas
description: Potatoes soaked then fried in olive oil, served with a smooth brava sauce of hot and sweet smoked paprika, cornstarch and vegetable broth.

ingredients.name: potato
ingredients.note: large Yukon Gold, peeled and cut into small pieces

ingredients.name: smoked paprika
ingredients.note: sweet smoked Spanish, for the sauce

ingredients.name: smoked paprika
ingredients.note: hot smoked Spanish, for the sauce

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: extra virgin, for frying the potatoes

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: sea salt, for the fried potatoes

steps.text: Peel and rinse the potatoes, cut them into small even pieces, and leave them in a bowl of cold water to release starch.
For the sauce, heat 1/4 cup oil in a pan over medium heat for about 3 minutes, then pour it into a bowl. Whisk in the two paprikas and the cornflour.
Return the mixture to the pan over medium heat and slowly pour in the broth, whisking constantly so it comes together.
Season the sauce with salt and white wine vinegar and keep whisking until creamy (about 10 minutes of cooking in all, per the video), then turn off the heat.
Drain the potatoes and pat completely dry. Heat 3/4 cup oil in a sauté pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes.
Fry the potatoes in the oil, stirring occasionally, until golden, about 20 minutes. Drain on paper towels and season with salt.
Rewarm the sauce on low heat for 2 minutes, whisking, then pour it generously over the potatoes and serve at once.

title: Gambas al ajillo
description: Garlic prawns: thinly sliced garlic and dried cayenne chillies browned gently in olive oil, then prawns cooked for a couple of minutes and finished with parsley.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: extra virgin, for frying; a good splash, enough to cover the base of the pan

ingredients.name: dried chillies
ingredients.note: whole dried cayenne chillies (cayenas); the description says 2–3

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: to taste, mixed into the prawns

steps.text: Peel the prawns and remove the vein. Peel the garlic and slice it very thinly and evenly.
Pour enough olive oil into a pan to cover the base. Add the cayenne chillies and the sliced garlic.
Cook over low heat, stirring, so the garlic turns golden without burning. Meanwhile salt the prawns to taste.
When the garlic is golden, add the prawns and spread them out in the oil. Cook for a couple of minutes at most.
Chop a handful of parsley and scatter it over. Serve with bread for dipping.

title: Spanish tortilla
description: A Spanish potato omelette: sliced potatoes fried slowly in olive oil, mixed into beaten eggs and cooked on low heat, flipped once so both sides set.

ingredients.name: potato
ingredients.note: large Yukon gold, peeled and thinly sliced

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: large, beaten with salt and pepper

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: extra virgin, for frying the potatoes

steps.text: Peel the potatoes, rinse and dry them, and slice each one thinly. Beat the eggs in a large bowl with sea salt and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a good nonstick pan over medium heat. After 2 minutes add the potato slices and stir now and then so they cook evenly.
After about 15 minutes season the potatoes with salt and pepper. Cook for around 25 minutes in total until they are perfectly cooked, then turn off the heat.
Tip the potatoes into the beaten eggs and mix well.
In the same pan on a low heat, add the egg and potato mixture. Run a spatula round the edge so it does not stick and shake the pan now and then.

After 4 minutes, put a plate bigger than the pan on top, flip the pan over and slide the uncooked side back in. Cook another 4 minutes, pressing the edges in with a spatula for a rounded shape, then slide onto a plate.

title: Easy fish pie
description: A white sauce with fish pie mix, sweetcorn, peas and chives under a mashed potato and cheddar topping, baked until golden.

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: for the sauce, plus a splash for the mash

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: for the sauce, plus a knob for the mash

ingredients.name: fish pie mix
ingredients.note: cod, salmon, smoked haddock etc; 320-400 g depending on pack

ingredients.name: chives
ingredients.note: finely snipped; half a 25 g pack, or a small bunch

ingredients.name: cheddar cheese
ingredients.note: grated; the video stirs some into the filling and keeps the rest for the top

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: to taste, for the filling and mash

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the peeled, halved potatoes in a pan, cover with cold water, bring to the boil and simmer until tender.
Meanwhile, put 25 g butter, the flour and the spring onions in another pan and heat gently, stirring, until the butter melts. Cook for 1-2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the 400 ml milk, bring to the boil while stirring, and cook for 3-4 minutes until smooth and thickened.
Off the heat, stir in the mustard, some of the cheddar (keep the rest for the top), the fish, chives, peas and sweetcorn. Season with black pepper and set aside.
Drain the potatoes and mash with a knob of butter, a splash of milk, salt and pepper until smooth.
Tip the filling into an ovenproof dish, cover with the mash, smoothing it right to the edges, and sprinkle with the remaining cheddar.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.

title: Toad in the hole
description: Chipolata sausages browned in the oven then baked in a puffed Yorkshire pudding batter, served with gravy and vegetables.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 C (200 C fan). Put the chipolatas in a 20 x 30 cm roasting tin with the oil and bake for 15 minutes until browned.
Meanwhile tip the flour into a bowl with the salt, make a well and crack in the eggs. Whisk with an electric whisk, slowly adding the milk, then leave the batter to stand.
Take the tin out of the oven, taking care as the fat is very hot; if it isn't sizzling, put it on the hob for a few minutes.
Pour the batter into the tin and bake on the top shelf for 25 to 30 minutes until risen and golden.
Serve with gravy and your favourite vegetables.

title: Red lentil chili
description: A plant-based chili of red lentils, tomatoes, red pepper and smoky spices, sweetened with blended dates and cooked in an electric pressure cooker, topped with scallions.

ingredients.name: dates
ingredients.note: about 9 Deglet Noor; blended with 1 cup of the water

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: divided; 1 cup for the dates, 6 for the pot

ingredients.name: canned tomatoes
ingredients.note: salt-free diced, 14.5 oz (411 g) each; fire roasted preferred

ingredients.name: tomato puree
ingredients.note: salt-free tomato paste, 6 oz (170 g) can

ingredients.name: red chilli flakes
ingredients.note: crushed red pepper flakes, or more to taste

ingredients.name: vegan parmesan
ingredients.note: faux Parmesan, to serve on top; the recipe is only linked

steps.text: Blend the dates with 1 cup of the water until smooth; a food processor gets it almost to a puree.
Put the date puree and all the remaining ingredients, including the other 6 cups of water, into an electric pressure cooker.
Cook on high for 10 minutes.
Or use a slow cooker instead: put everything in with 6 cups of water in total and cook on low for 8 hours.
Sprinkle with chopped scallions and serve with baked tortilla chips or over a baked potato.

title: Salmon avocado salad
description: Pan-fried salmon fillets on a salad of avocado, cucumber and mixed leaves, dressed with a mint, lime and honey dressing.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: a little extra, to rub on the salmon

ingredients.name: lime
ingredients.note: zest of 1 and juice of limes for the dressing; number of limes juiced is garbled in the source

steps.text: Season the salmon fillets and rub them with a little oil.
Mix the mint, lime zest and juice, honey and olive oil together for the dressing.
Halve, stone, peel and slice the avocados. Cut the cucumber in half and then into quarters lengthways, and slice.
Divide the salad leaves, avocado and cucumber between four plates and drizzle with half the dressing.
Heat a non-stick pan and fry the salmon for 3-4 minutes on each side, until crisp outside but still moist inside.
Put a salmon fillet on top of each salad, drizzle with the rest of the dressing and serve warm.

title: Creamy tomato soup
description: A small-batch smooth tomato soup made from fresh tomatoes, onion, garlic and carrot, sieved and finished with a spoonful of cream.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: ½ tsp while cooking the tomatoes, ¼ tsp added at the end

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: ½ cup to boil the tomatoes, ½ cup or more added after sieving; the recipe's ingredient list says 1 cup

ingredients.name: cream
ingredients.note: stirred in at the end; extra cream to garnish

steps.text: Heat the butter in a pan and saute the onion, garlic and bay leaf.
Add the chopped tomatoes, carrot and 1/2 tsp salt and saute for a minute, until the tomatoes change colour.
Add 1/2 cup water, cover and boil for about 10 minutes until the tomatoes are soft and mushy.
Remove the bay leaf and let the mixture cool, then blend it to a smooth paste without adding water.
Sieve the paste, discarding the residue, and stir in another 1/2 cup water, or more to adjust the thickness.
Bring the soup to a boil and mix in the sugar, crushed pepper and 1/4 tsp more salt.
Turn off the heat and stir in the cream. Serve garnished with a mint leaf and a little more cream.

title: Pancakes
description: Simple American-style pancakes from a flour, milk, egg and baking powder batter, cooked on a lightly oiled griddle or frying pan.

ingredients.name: baking powder
ingredients.note: the narrator says tablespoons, but the description and written recipe correct this to teaspoons

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: in the batter, plus a little to oil the pan

steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl and make a well in the centre.
Pour in the milk, beaten egg and oil and mix until the batter is smooth.
Heat a griddle or frying pan over medium-high heat and oil it lightly.
Pour or scoop about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake onto the griddle.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until small bubbles form in the centre and the edges are brown and dry, then flip.
Cook until browned on the other side, then repeat with the remaining batter and serve hot.

title: Banana pancakes
description: Small, delicate two-ingredient pancakes made from mashed ripe banana and beaten eggs, fried in a little coconut oil.

ingredients.name: coconut oil
ingredients.note: a little, for the pan (the written recipe says oil or butter)

steps.text: Mash the banana in a large bowl until fairly smooth; a few lumps are fine.
Beat in the eggs until the batter is smooth and small bubbles appear. A fork, whisk or blender all work.
Heat a little coconut oil in a large frying pan.
Drop 2 tablespoons of batter per pancake into the hot pan and keep them small, as they are very delicate.
Cook until bubbles appear on the surface, then flip and cook through on both sides.
Serve plain or topped with ice cream, cream, maple syrup or honey.

title: Smoked salmon eggs Benedict
description: Poached eggs and smoked salmon on thick slices of toast, covered with a lemony hollandaise made over a double boiler and finished with chopped parsley.

ingredients.name: white pepper
ingredients.note: for the hollandaise; transcript says about 1/4 tsp

ingredients.name: egg yolks
ingredients.note: from large eggs, for the hollandaise

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: room temperature, whisked in off the heat

ingredients.name: bread
ingredients.note: thick, toasted; 1 per serving, pain de mie works well

ingredients.name: parsley
ingredients.note: leaves only, finely chopped, to garnish

steps.text: Beat the egg yolks with the white pepper until frothy and slightly thick, about 1 minute. Whisk in the lemon juice and water.

Bring about 1 cup of water to the boil in the bottom pan of a double boiler and nest the pan of yolk mixture on top. Add 1 tablespoon of butter and whisk constantly; when the water boils again, turn the heat to low and keep whisking until it thickens, which happens quickly. Keep it below about 66°C so the yolks don't scramble.
Take it off the heat and whisk in the room-temperature butter about a tablespoon at a time, fully mixing each addition before the next. Taste and whisk in the salt, then cover and keep warm.
Bring several cups of water with the white vinegar to a boil in a large sauté pan, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Toast thick slices of bread (about 2 cm). Chop the parsley leaves finely.
Break each egg into a small bowl and ease it into the simmering water close to the surface. Poach for 3 minutes, then lift out with a slotted spoon onto paper towel.
Put a slice of smoked salmon on each toast, top with a poached egg and spoon over plenty of warm hollandaise. Garnish with chopped parsley.

title: Key lime pie
description: A pie with a flaky shortening crust blind-baked first, filled with a baked lime, egg and sweetened condensed milk custard, and served cold with sweetened whipped cream and lime zest.

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: pastry flour, for the crust; half of the 2 cups said, since the video makes a double batch of dough and fills only one crust

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the crust; half of the 1 tsp said (double batch)

ingredients.name: shortening
ingredients.note: for the crust; half of the 3/4 cup said (double batch)

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: ice cold, added gradually; half of 5 tbsp plus 1 tbsp said (double batch)

ingredients.name: lime
ingredients.note: microwaved 10 seconds and rolled, then juiced for about 1/2 cup of juice

ingredients.name: food colouring
ingredients.note: green, optional, for a pale lime green

ingredients.name: lime
ingredients.note: zest shaved on top, to garnish

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 C. Cut the shortening into the flour and salt with a pastry cutter until it looks like gravel.
Sprinkle in the ice water a little at a time, mixing gently with a fork until the dough just comes together, then form a loose ball without kneading. Skip resting.
Press the dough into a round, roll it out 3-6 mm thick and a couple of inches wider than the pie tin, fold it into the tin, tuck under the excess and crimp the edge. Prick the base with a fork.
Blind-bake in the middle of the oven for 10-12 minutes until lightly golden, then cool completely.
Microwave the limes for about 10 seconds, roll them on the bench, then juice them to get about 1/2 cup.
Mix the eggs, condensed milk and lime juice with a mixer, plus a drop of green food colouring if you like, until it is a pale lime green.
Pour the filling into the cooled crust and bake at 175 C for about 30 minutes, until just set. Overcooking makes it tough and bitter.
Cool the pie for at least an hour, then chill it and serve cold with sweetened whipped cream and lime zest.

title: New York cheesecake
description: Dense, creamy and impossibly smooth baked cheesecake.

steps.text: Position an oven shelf in the middle of the oven. Preheat the oven to fan 160C/conventional 180C/gas 4. Line the base of a 23cm springform cake tin with parchment paper. For the crust, melt the butter in a medium pan.
Stir in the biscuit crumbs and sugar so the mixture is evenly moistened. Press the mixture into the bottom of the pan and bake for 10 minutes. Cool on a wire rack while preparing the filling.

For the filling, increase the oven temperature to fan 200C/conventional 240C/gas 9. In a table top mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, beat the soft cheese at medium-low speed until creamy, about 2 minutes.
With the mixer on low, gradually add the sugar, then the flour and a pinch of salt, scraping down the sides of the bowl and the paddle twice.
Swap the paddle attachment for the whisk. Continue by adding the vanilla, lemon zest and juice. Whisk in the eggs and yolk, one at a time, scraping the bowl and whisk at least twice.

Stir the 284ml carton of soured cream until smooth, then measure 200ml/7fl oz (just over 3⁄4 of the carton). Continue on low speed as you add the measured soured cream (reserve the rest). Whisk to blend, but don't over-beat.
The batter should be smooth, light and somewhat airy.

Brush the sides of the springform tin with melted butter and put on a baking sheet. Pour in the filling - if there are any lumps, sink them using a knife - the top should be as smooth as possible. Bake for 10 minutes.
Reduce oven temperature to fan 90C/conventional 110C/gas 1⁄4 and bake for 25 minutes more. If you gently shake the tin, the filling should have a slight wobble.

Turn off the oven and open the oven door for a cheesecake that's creamy in the centre, or leave it closed if you prefer a drier texture. Let cool in the oven for 2 hours. The cheesecake may get a slight crack on top as it cools.

Combine the reserved soured cream with the 142ml carton, the sugar and lemon juice for the topping. Spread over the cheesecake right to the edges. Cover loosely with foil and refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight.

Run a round-bladed knife around the sides of the tin to loosen any stuck edges. Unlock the side, slide the cheesecake off the bottom of the tin onto a plate, then slide the parchment paper out from underneath.

title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
description: Soft date sponge made with mashed dates, baked in one tin, soaked with butterscotch sauce and served warm with more sauce and ice cream.

ingredients.name: brown sugar
ingredients.note: tightly packed, for the butterscotch sauce

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and line a 20 cm square cake tin with overhanging paper.
Put the chopped dates in a bowl, sprinkle over the bicarbonate of soda and pour on the boiling water. Leave for 10 minutes, then mash to a thick, sloppy porridge.
Beat the 1/4 cup brown sugar and softened butter until smooth, beat in the eggs, then mix in the flour and baking powder.
Mix in the mashed dates quickly until combined, pour into the tin, level and bake for 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Make the butterscotch sauce: put the 1 cup brown sugar, cream, vanilla and butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Once the butter melts, stir, bring to a simmer and cook 2 minutes.
While the pudding is hot, poke about 40 holes in it with a skewer and pour over 1/2 cup of the sauce. Leave to soak for 10 minutes.
Lift out with the paper overhang, cut and serve warm with the remaining warm sauce and ice cream or cream.

title: Chocolate layer cake with chocolate cream cheese frosting
description: A cocoa cake made with buttermilk and warm water, baked in three 23 cm pans and put together with a chocolate cream cheese buttercream. Makes one three-layer cake.

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: all-purpose; plus a little to dust the pans

ingredients.name: icing sugar
ingredients.note: powdered; 7-8 cups, added 1 cup at a time

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: about, as needed for the frosting

steps.text: Heat the oven to 176°C. Butter three 23 cm (9-inch) cake pans, dust them with flour (or cocoa) and tap out the excess.
Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, bicarbonate of soda, baking powder and salt together in a large bowl or stand mixer.
Add the eggs, buttermilk, warm water, oil and vanilla and mix until smooth, without overmixing. Scrape the bowl so no dry cocoa or flour is left.
Divide the batter evenly among the three pans, a little over 3 cups each.
Bake on the centre rack for 30-35 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pans on wire racks for about 10-15 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.
For the frosting, beat the butter and cream cheese until light and fluffy, then beat in the cocoa and vanilla.
Beat in the powdered sugar a cup at a time, adding milk as needed to get a thick, spreadable frosting.
Once the cakes are completely cool, put the three layers together with the frosting.

title: Tarte Tatin
description: Apples cooked in a sugar, water and butter caramel in a skillet, topped with a sheet of puff pastry, baked and turned out upside down.

ingredients.name: apple
ingredients.note: firm baking apples such as Granny Smith or Honeycrisp, peeled, quartered and cored; recipe says 4 to 5

ingredients.name: puff pastry
ingredients.note: 1 sheet, rolled out slightly and cut to an 11-inch (28 cm) circle

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 C. Peel, quarter and core the apples and set them aside.

In a 10-inch (25 cm) oven-proof skillet, sprinkle the sugar over the base and drizzle with the water. Cook over medium heat, stirring now and then, until it bubbles and turns light amber, 5-7 minutes.
Stir in the butter until melted; it will bubble up, so take care.
Add the apples and cook, stirring every few minutes, for about 15 minutes until the caramel is deep amber. Take off the heat and arrange the apples curved side down in concentric circles.
Roll the puff pastry out slightly, cut an 11-inch (28 cm) circle and lay it over the apples, tucking the edges down. Put the skillet on a rimmed baking sheet.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden brown on top.
Cool on a wire rack for 15 minutes (up to 30 in a cast-iron skillet), then carefully invert onto a rimmed serving plate.

title: Portuguese custard tarts
description: Pastéis de nata made with a laminated butter dough rolled into a log, sliced and pressed into a tin, filled with a cinnamon sugar-syrup custard and baked very hot until blistered.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: unsalted, very soft, spread over the dough in three layers

ingredients.name: plain flour
ingredients.note: extra, for dusting and rolling the dough

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: whisked with the flour for the custard

ingredients.name: cinnamon stick
ingredients.note: removed from the syrup at 100 C

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: brought to the boil and poured over the flour paste

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt and water with a dough hook for a couple of minutes into a very sticky dough that pulls away from the bowl. Scrape it onto a heavily floured surface, shape into a rough square, flour the top, wrap in cling film and rest for 10 minutes.

Roll the dough into a 16 x 16 inch (about 40 cm) square and brush off excess flour. Dot a third of the soft butter over two thirds of it, leaving a gap at the edges, fold the buttered third over the middle, then fold the plain third over the top.
Turn the strip 90 degrees, roll it to a 16 x 16 inch (about 40 cm) square again and repeat the buttering and folding with a second third of the butter.

Roll to an 18 x 21 inch (about 46 x 53 cm) rectangle, trim the edges and spread the last of the butter over the whole sheet. Roll it up tightly into a log, trim the ends and cut it in half; each half makes 12 pastries. Wrap in cling film and chill for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.

For the custard, whisk the 40 g flour with the 50 ml milk until smooth. Heat the water, caster sugar and cinnamon stick over low heat, without stirring, to 100 C, and bring the 250 ml milk to the boil in another pan.
Pour the boiling milk onto the flour paste, whisking, and add the vanilla. Remove the cinnamon stick from the syrup and pour the syrup in a steady stream into the milk mixture, whisking.
Stir for 10-15 minutes until warm rather than hot, then whisk in the egg yolks and strain through a sieve into a jug. Cover and set aside; the video uses only half of it.
Cut a chilled log into 12 slices, about 2.5-4 cm thick, and put one in each hole of a lightly greased 12-hole cupcake tin. Leave at room temperature for 10-15 minutes to soften.
With wet thumbs and fingers, press each slice into a disc and draw it up the sides to form a cup, keeping the base from getting too thin. Fill about three-quarters full with custard.
Bake in an oven at its highest setting (280 C in the video) for 8-9 minutes, watching closely, until the tops are blistered and dark. Serve with icing sugar and cinnamon sprinkled on top.

title: Eton mess
description: Crushed meringue layered with whipped cream and a chunky lemony strawberry mixture in clear glasses.

ingredients.name: meringue nests
ingredients.note: vanilla meringue cookies, 10-12 (3-4 oz, about 85-115 g)

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: granulated; 3-4 tbsp total, 2-3 for the strawberries and 1 for the cream

steps.text: Put the meringues in a zip-top bag and crush them into coarse crumbles with a rolling pin.
Toss two thirds of the sliced strawberries with the lemon zest, lemon juice and 2-3 tbsp sugar, depending on how sweet the berries are.
Coarsely mash the strawberries with a potato masher or immersion blender into a chunky mixture, then stir in the remaining quartered strawberries. Add more sugar to taste.
Beat the cold cream with 1 tbsp sugar on medium-high speed for 3-4 minutes until whipped and spreadable.
Layer cream, strawberry mixture and meringue in glasses or dishes, then repeat to fill them.

title: Apple & Blackberry Crumble
description: Jammy fruit under a buttery, golden crumble.

steps.text: Heat oven to 190C/170C fan/gas 5. Tip the flour and sugar into a large bowl. Add the butter, then rub into the flour using your fingertips to make a light breadcrumb texture. Do not overwork it or the crumble will become heavy.
Sprinkle the mixture evenly over a baking sheet and bake for 15 mins or until lightly coloured.

Meanwhile, for the compote, peel, core and cut the apples into 2cm dice. Put the butter and sugar in a medium saucepan and melt together over a medium heat. Cook for 3 mins until the mixture turns to a light caramel.
Stir in the apples and cook for 3 mins. Add the blackberries and cinnamon, and cook for 3 mins more. Cover, remove from the heat, then leave for 2-3 mins to continue cooking in the warmth of the pan.
To serve, spoon the warm fruit into an ovenproof gratin dish, top with the crumble mix, then reheat in the oven for 5-10 mins. Serve with vanilla ice cream.

title: Chocolate Raspberry Brownies
description: Fudgy brownies made by melting semisweet chocolate with butter, whisking in sugar and eggs, then folding in chopped chocolate and fresh raspberries before baking.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: plus a little to grease the pan

ingredients.name: dark chocolate
ingredients.note: semisweet chips or chunks, folded into the batter

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C. Butter an 8-inch (20 cm) square pan and line it with parchment.
Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl over simmering water, stirring until smooth. Turn off the heat, keep the bowl over the water and stir in the sugar, then lift it off.
Whisk in the eggs one at a time until combined, then stir in the vanilla. Add the flour, salt and cocoa and stir well.
Stir in the chopped chocolate and the fresh raspberries.
Pour the batter into the pan and bake for 25-30 minutes, until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely, lift out with the parchment and cut into squares.

title: Anzac biscuits
description: Oat and coconut biscuits sweetened with golden syrup, made by stirring bicarbonate-frothed melted butter into the dry mix and baking spoonfuls on lined trays at 180°C.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: white, 1 cup; for chewier biscuits use ½ cup white and ½ cup brown sugar

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and prepare two baking trays.
Mix the oats, coconut, sifted flour, sugar and salt in a bowl.
Melt the butter, then stir in the golden syrup, bicarbonate of soda and boiling water.
Pour the liquid into the dry ingredients and mix well.
Spoon the mixture onto lined trays and bake for 10–12 minutes.
Loosen the biscuits on the tray with a knife or spatula and leave them to cool on the tray.

title: Lamingtons
description: Squares of vanilla sponge dipped in a thin chocolate icing and rolled in desiccated coconut, with no cream or jam filling.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 C. Grease a 23 cm square tin and line it with baking paper.
Beat the eggs, sugar and vanilla in a large bowl until light and fluffy.
Sift in the flour and baking powder and mix just until combined, then mix in the melted butter.
Pour into the tin and bake for 25 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.
Mix the melted butter and warm milk for the icing, then sift in the cocoa and icing sugar and mix until smooth.
Once the cake is chilled, trim the edges and cut it into squares. Put the coconut in a bowl.
Using a fork, dip each square in the chocolate icing, turn to coat and let it drain, then roll in the coconut and set on a wire rack.
Refrigerate the lamingtons for about 15 minutes until set, then serve.

title: Aussie Burgers
description: Beef mince patties topped with melted cheddar, bacon, a fried egg, canned beetroot, pineapple, lettuce, tomato and ketchup in a burger bun (brioche is best). Makes 4 burgers.

ingredients.name: bacon
ingredients.note: shortcut bacon, or two full rashers

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: optional, for spreading on the toasted buns, to serve

steps.text: Season the beef mince with salt and pepper and form it into four patties.
Fry the patties in the oil until cooked through, then top each with a slice of cheddar to melt.
Fry the bacon and the eggs the way you like them.
If you like, toast the buns and spread them with butter.
Fill each bun with a cheese-topped patty, bacon, a fried egg, a pineapple ring, three slices of beetroot, ketchup, tomato and lettuce.

title: Chicken & chorizo rice pot
description: One-pot chicken thigh and chorizo rice with peppers, carrot, mushrooms, peas and basmati, simmered in tomato and paprika stock and rested covered.

ingredients.name: basmati rice
ingredients.note: brown or white; rinsed well and drained

ingredients.name: chorizo
ingredients.note: thinly sliced; the video uses an Angus beef chorizo

ingredients.name: chilli
ingredients.note: finely sliced, optional (video uses about half)

ingredients.name: green olives
ingredients.note: optional, flesh cut away from the stone; colour not stated

ingredients.name: tomato puree
ingredients.note: tomato paste, whisked into the stock

steps.text: Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water and leave it to drain.
Heat the oil in a large lidded pot. Sauté the chicken strips over high heat for 30-40 seconds a side and set aside.
Sauté the chorizo for 1 minute and add it to the chicken.
In the same pot cook the onion, pepper, carrot and chilli for 2-3 minutes. Lower the heat, add the garlic and cook 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, olives and peas. Whisk the stock with the tomato paste and paprika and pour it in.
Return the chicken and chorizo, add the rice and salt, and stir while bringing to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook 15 minutes.
Take off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes without lifting the lid. Serve.

title: Tofu, greens & cashew stir-fry
description: Crisp tofu, greens and cashews in a quick garlicky sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a non-stick wok. Add the broccoli, then fry on a high heat for 5 mins or until just tender, adding a little water if it begins to catch.
Add the garlic and chilli, fry for 1 min, then toss through the spring onions, soya beans, pak choi and tofu. Stir-fry for 2-3 mins. Add the hoisin, soy and nuts to warm through.

title: Vietnamese grilled pork
description: Caramelised grilled pork over rice noodles with herbs and nuoc cham.

steps.text: Slice the uncooked pork thinly, about ⅛". It helps to slightly freeze it (optional).
Mince garlic and shallots. Mix in a bowl with sugar, fish sauce, thick soy sauce, pepper, and oil until sugar dissolves.
Marinate the meat for 1 hour, or overnight for better results.
Bake the pork at 375F for 10-15 minutes or until about 80% cooked. Finish cooking by broiling in the oven until a nice golden brown color develops, flipping the pieces midway.
Assemble your bowl with veggies, noodles, and garnish. Many like to mix the whole bowl up and pour the fish sauce on top, but I like to make individual bites and sauce it slowly.

title: Acaraje black-eyed pea fritters with shrimp filling
description: A Brazilian dish of prawns, black-eyed peas and chilli — serves 6, on the table in about 45 minutes.

steps.text: Make the filling by placing the onion, ginger, garlic, chilli, and some salt into food processor. Purée until smooth. Heat the oil in a frying pan and pour the purée into it. Fry for 5 mins or until cooked through.
Add the prawns, tomatoes and chopped coriander. Squeeze in the lime and add salt to taste. Cook for 3 mins, or until the prawns have cooked through. Remove from the heat.

Drain and rinse the black-eyed peas. Pour into a food processor with the garlic and chili. Purée until smooth. Scrape into a bowl and add the onion, flour, salt, chilli powder and baking powder. Mix and roll into 16 balls.
Heat the oven to 190C/170C fan/gas 5. Heat 8cm of the palm or vegetable oil in a wok or small heavy pan. When a small piece of bread sizzles, drop 4-5 balls into the oil.

Fry until golden and crisp, about 4-5 mins. Drain on kitchen paper and repeat until they are all finished. You can keep them warm in the oven while you finish. Slice the fritters open down the centre and spoon the prawn filling in. Serve with hot sauce.

title: Adana kebab
description: Hand-minced lamb and lamb tail fat seasoned only with salt and paprika, moulded onto flat skewers and grilled over charcoal. Served on lavash with onion salad, roasted tomatoes and chillies.

ingredients.name: lamb
ingredients.note: belly, ribs or top round; sinew removed

ingredients.name: lamb fat
ingredients.note: tail fat, 50–100 g depending on the fat in the meat

ingredients.name: capsicum
ingredients.note: optional; medium red pepper, finely chopped and squeezed dry

ingredients.name: tomato
ingredients.note: roasted on the grill, to serve

ingredients.name: chilli
ingredients.note: colour not stated; roasted on the grill, to serve

steps.text: Remove the sinew and connective tissue from the lamb and cut it into smaller pieces. Rest it in the fridge overnight, then freeze it for 30 minutes before chopping.
If the meat is lean (for example leg), chop in lamb tail fat so the total fat is 15–30%.
Mince the meat and fat with a large cleaver or mezzaluna, being careful to cut rather than smash it.
Add 1 tsp salt and 2 tsp paprika, plus the chopped, squeezed red pepper if using. Mix gently and keep chopping until everything is combined.
Divide the mixture into 120–150 g portions and cool them in the fridge. Chill the skewers too, so the kebabs hold on them.
With wet fingers, push each portion onto a large flat skewer, pressing gently to spread it evenly and sealing the ends. Keep the skewered kebabs in the fridge or freezer for 20–30 minutes.
Light the charcoal grill and roast the tomatoes and chillies first.
When the charcoal is medium hot, grill the kebabs, turning them after 30–60 seconds once the underside has set so the meat doesn't fall off.
After 2–3 minutes, when the fat starts dripping, lift the kebabs off and rest them on lavash to soak up the excess fat, which also stops flare-ups.
Finish grilling, turning often, for 3–4 minutes a side (6–8 minutes in total).
Serve on a large platter over lavash with onion salad, roasted tomatoes and chillies.

title: Air Fryer Egg Rolls
description: Egg rolls filled with browned ground pork, cabbage, spring onion, garlic and ginger, rolled in wrappers, sprayed with oil and air-fried until crisp.

ingredients.name: pork mince
ingredients.note: ground pork; ground turkey or beef also works

ingredients.name: cabbage
ingredients.note: coleslaw mix, or sliced cabbage with grated carrot

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: cooking spray, olive oil mister or brushed oil, for greasing the rolls before air frying

steps.text: Chop the spring onions and press or mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pork, break it up and cook, stirring often, for about 4 minutes until well browned with few pink pieces left.
Add the coleslaw mix, spring onion, garlic and ginger. Cook, stirring now and then, for about 2 minutes until tender.
Stir in the soy sauce and sesame oil, then let the filling cool for a minute or two.
Brush two edges of an egg roll wrapper with water, put 2 to 3 tbsp filling diagonally in the middle, fold in the two wet corners, then roll up. Repeat, keeping the wrappers covered with a damp towel.
Spray the tops of half the rolls with oil and place them oiled side down in the air fryer basket with space between them. Spray the tops too.
Air fry at 175 C for 7 minutes, flip, spray again and cook about 5 more minutes. Repeat with the second batch.
Serve warm with your favourite dipping sauce.

title: Air fryer patatas bravas
description: Boiled then air-fried potato cubes served with a quick uncooked salsa brava of olive oil, vinegar, garlic and hot paprika, and a garlic alioli.

ingredients.name: potato
ingredients.note: Maris Piper, peeled and cut into chunky bite-sized cubes

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: for the boiling water, to taste

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: extra virgin, for the salsa brava

ingredients.name: worcestershire sauce
ingredients.note: or chilli powder, for the salsa brava

steps.text: Cut the peeled potatoes into chunky bite-sized cubes. Boil them in salted water for about 5 minutes.
Drain well and let the steam dry off for a few minutes. Toss with the oil and salt.
Spread in a single layer in the air fryer basket and cook at 200°C for 20–25 minutes, shaking halfway through, until golden and crisp.
For the salsa brava, mix the oil, vinegar, garlic, Worcestershire sauce or chilli powder, hot paprika and salt in a bowl.
For the alioli, mix the mayonnaise, garlic, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Pile the potatoes on a plate, spoon over the salsa brava and serve the alioli alongside or drizzled over.

title: Ají de Aguacate (Colombian Spicy Avocado Sauce)
description: A Colombian dish of avocado, scotch bonnet and lime — serves 2, ready in under half an hour.

steps.text: Place all the ingredients in a food processor. Process until the mixture is well combined.
If the mixture is too thick, add more lime juice until you reach the desired consistency.

title: Ajo blanco
description: Chilled Spanish almond and garlic soup: blanched almonds, soaked baguette, olive oil and red wine vinegar blended smooth and chilled, served with peeled green grapes.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: cold; 2 cups in the ingredient list: 1 cup for soaking the bread, 1 cup to blend

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: extra virgin, plus a little to drizzle

ingredients.name: green grapes
ingredients.note: seedless, halved and skinned, to garnish

steps.text: Soak the 4 slices of baguette in 1 cup of cold water for about 10 minutes.
Put the almonds, soaked bread, garlic, red wine vinegar, olive oil, 1/2 tsp sea salt and 1 cup cold water in a tall container.
Blend with a hand mixer for about 3 minutes, until a smooth purée.
Cover and chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Halve about 10 seedless green grapes and peel off the skins.
Stir the chilled soup and pour into 2 shallow bowls. Top with the grapes and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.

title: Alfajores
description: Argentine cornflour (maicena) sandwich biscuits: a crumbly, pale dough baked briefly, filled with dulce de leche and rolled in desiccated coconut.

ingredients.name: dulce de leche
ingredients.note: ideally the thick 'repostero' type, for the filling

ingredients.name: desiccated coconut
ingredients.note: for rolling the edges (c/n, as needed)

steps.text: Beat the softened butter with the icing sugar until creamy, then beat in the eggs.
Add the cognac, vanilla and lemon zest and beat again until combined.
Gradually sift in the flour, cornflour, baking powder and salt. Mix until a smooth, even dough forms.
Wrap the dough in cling film and chill for about 30 minutes so it is easy to work.
Dust the bench and dough with flour and roll the dough to about 5 mm thick. Cut out 5 cm rounds and place them on a baking tray. Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Bake at 180°C for 5–8 minutes. The biscuits should be cooked but still pale, and small cracks on top are normal. Cool completely.
Pipe or spread dulce de leche on the underside of one biscuit, about as thick as the biscuit, and press a second one on top.
Roll the edges of each alfajor in desiccated coconut until well coated.

title: Algerian Bouzgene Berber Bread with Roasted Pepper Sauce
description: An Algerian side of capsicum, tomato and jalapeño — makes 12, on the table in about 45 minutes.

steps.text: Preheat your oven's broiler. Place red bell peppers and tomatoes on a baking sheet, and roast under the broiler for about 8 minutes, turning occasionally. This should blacken the skin and help it peel off more easily.
Cool, then scrape the skins off of the tomatoes and peppers, and place them in a large bowl. Remove cores and seeds from the bell peppers.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the jalapenos and garlic, and cook until tender, stirring frequently. Remove from heat, and transfer the garlic and jalapeno to the bowl with the tomatoes and red peppers.
Using two sharp steak knives (one in each hand), cut up the tomatoes and peppers to a coarse and soupy consistency. Stir, and set sauce aside.

Place the semolina in a large bowl, and stir in salt and 4 tablespoons of olive oil. Gradually add water while mixing and squeezing with your hand until the dough holds together without being sticky or dry, and molds easily with the hand.
Divide into 6 pieces and form into balls.
For each round, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large heavy skillet over medium heat. Roll out dough one round at a time, to no thicker than 1/4 inch.
Fry in the hot skillet until dark brown spots appear on the surface, and they are crispy. Remove from the skillet, and wrap in a clean towel while preparing the remaining flat breads.
To eat the bread and sauce, break off pieces of the bread, and scoop them into the sauce. It will slide off, but just keep reaching in!

title: Algerian Carrots
description: An Algerian side of carrot, cinnamon and ground cumin — serves 4, about an hour start to finish.

steps.text: Place a steamer insert into a saucepan, and fill with 1 1/2 cups of water, or just below the bottom of the steamer. Cover, and bring the water to a boil over high heat.

Add the sliced carrots, reduce the heat to medium, and cover the pan again. Steam until tender but not mushy, 4 to 6 minutes depending on the thickness of the slices. Reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and stir in the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cumin, garlic, and thyme. Cook the spices and garlic, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 10 minutes.
Add the 1/2 cup reserved cooking liquid and the bay leaf, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the carrots, tossing well to coat with the spice mixture, and cook until heated through, about 2 to 3 minutes. Sprinkle with lemon juice and remove the bay leaf before serving.

title: Algerian Flafla (Bell Pepper Salad)
description: An Algerian salad of capsicum, red onion and tomato — serves 2, about an hour start to finish.

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 230°C (450°F) (230 degrees C). Place the whole peppers on aluminum foil. Bake until the skin is spotted black and the peppers are soft, 30 to 45 minutes, turning the peppers once if necessary.
Remove peppers from the oven and set aside to cool for 10 minutes. Peel off the skin and remove the stem and seeds. Chop the roasted peppers into half-inch pieces.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the onion and cook, stirring frequently, until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, salt, and pepper; stir in the chopped peppers and tomato. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the tomato is soft and the mixture is well incorporated, about 5 minutes.

title: Algerian Kefta (Meatballs)
description: Lean beef meatballs seasoned with garlic and onion, pan-fried and served in a garlicky fresh plum tomato sauce with ras el hanout, with crusty bread or rice. Makes about 12 to 14 meatballs.

steps.text: Mix the beef, garlic and onion for the meatballs with your hands until combined.
Shape into oblong patties about 1.5 inches (4 cm) long, making 12 to 14.
Cook the patties in a large skillet over medium-high heat, in batches if needed, until crisp on both sides and no longer pink, about 10 minutes in total.
Move the meatballs to a serving dish. Lower the heat to medium and cook the onion for the sauce in the drippings with salt and pepper, stirring, until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, parsley, ras el hanout and water. Cook until the tomatoes are soft, about 5 minutes.
Spoon the sauce over the meatballs and serve with crusty bread or rice.

title: Almojábanas (Colombian Cheese Bread)
description: A Colombian side of cornmeal, queso fresco and mozzarella — serves 4, on the table in about 45 minutes.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F)
Mix the masarepa and cheese in a food processor.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix well.
Divide into 8 equal-size portions and shape into a ball.
Place on a greased baking sheet and bake for about 25 to 30 minutes, or until they are golden. Serve warm.

title: Amok Trey – Cambodian Fish Curry
description: A Cambodian curry with white fish, fish sauce and coconut milk — serves 4, about an hour start to finish.

steps.text: In a medium bowl, combine the coconut milk, red curry paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, and broth, whisking until smooth—this ensures no lumps in the sauce.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat (about 180°C (350°F)) for 30 seconds until shimmering.
Pour the coconut milk mixture into the skillet and bring it to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally, which should take about 3-4 minutes.
Add the fish cubes and kaffir lime leaves to the skillet, submerging them fully in the sauce.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the skillet, and let it cook for 10 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork—avoid overcooking to keep it tender.
Stir in the beaten egg slowly, cooking for 2 more minutes until the sauce thickens slightly, which adds a rich, custard-like texture.
While the curry simmers, prepare the banana leaves by briefly passing them over a gas flame for 10 seconds to make them pliable, or use parchment paper as a handy alternative.
Spoon the curry into the center of each banana leaf square, folding the edges to form a tight packet to trap steam.
Place the packets in a steamer basket over boiling water and steam for 10 minutes until heated through and fragrant.
Carefully unwrap the packets and garnish with fresh cilantro and lime wedges before serving.

title: Antiguan Breakfast (Chop Up and ‘Saltfish’)
description: An Antiguan breakfast of aubergine, callaloo and pumpkin — serves 2, ready in under half an hour.

steps.text: Peel and chop eggplant and pumpkin into medium-sized pieces.
Heat butter and add onions and garlic in a medium sized pot set to medium to high heat. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened but not browned.
Add pumpkin and eggplant. Sauté for an additional two to three minutes.
Add water just to cover the vegetables. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to a simmer and cook until the vegetables are soft.
Add the chopped spinach, stir and cook for an additional 3 minutes.
Pour the vegetable mixture into a colander and let drain.
After vegetable mixture has been drained return it to the pot and mash vigorously with a potato masher or a thick whisk.
Add salt and pepper. Adjust seasoning to taste.

title: Apam balik
description: A thin, crispy Malaysian peanut pancake from a rested plain and rice flour batter, cooked in a small pan with sugar, roasted peanuts, sweetcorn and butter, then folded in half.

ingredients.name: baking powder
ingredients.note: 1 tsp is the creator's written (corrected) amount; she marks this line 'Error on video'

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: room temperature, about 65 g with shell

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: granulated, to taste, for the filling

ingredients.name: peanuts
ingredients.note: roasted and chopped, to taste, for the filling

ingredients.name: sweetcorn
ingredients.note: or creamed corn, to taste, for the filling

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: unsalted, to taste, for the filling

steps.text: Whisk all the batter ingredients (both flours, sugar, bicarbonate of soda, salt, baking powder, egg and water) together just until combined with no lumps.
Cover tightly with cling film and rest the batter for 30 minutes in a warm, draught-free place. Whisk again before using, adding a splash of water if it is too thick.

Lightly oil a small non-stick pan (about 5 inches) over moderate heat. When hot, pour in the batter to coat the pan, using the back of a small round bowl to spread it evenly. Use less batter for a thinner pancake.
Cook for about 1 minute, until the batter sets and small bubbles form.
Sprinkle on plenty of granulated sugar, then the chopped roasted peanuts, then several teaspoons of sweetcorn, with the unsalted butter.
Keep cooking until the pancake is light golden, then loosen the edges with a palette knife.
Fold the pancake in half, move it to a plate and serve warm.

title: Apple cake
description: A Dutch sweet made with self-raising flour, apple and cinnamon — serves 8, about an hour start to finish.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180°C. (350°F) Grease a cake pan and line it with baking paper.
In a large bowl, break the four eggs with the sugar and beat until they have tripled in volume and become fluffy.
Sift the self-rising baking flour and add it to your egg mixture. Fold this over, preserving as much air as possible. Add the melted (and slightly cooled) butter and mix until combined.
Add cinnamon, pinch of salt and vanilla extract.
Add the diced apple to the batter and gently fold them into the batter so that the apple pieces are evenly distributed. You can roll the apple pieces through some more cinnamon.
Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
Place the apple slices on top of the batter and press lightly. Sprinkle optionally with some almond shavings.
Bake the apple cake in the preheated oven for about 45-50 minutes, or until a wooden skewer comes out clean when inserted into the center of the cake.
Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool in the mold for a few minutes. Then carefully remove the cake from the mold and let cool completely on a wire rack.
Sprinkle the cooled apple cake with powdered sugar.

title: Apple Frangipan Tart
description: A British sweet made with digestive biscuits, apple and almonds — serves 8, about an hour start to finish.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200C/180C Fan/Gas 6.
Put the biscuits in a large re-sealable freezer bag and bash with a rolling pin into fine crumbs. Melt the butter in a small pan, then add the biscuit crumbs and stir until coated with butter.
Tip into the tart tin and, using the back of a spoon, press over the base and sides of the tin to give an even layer. Chill in the fridge while you make the filling.

Cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. You can do this in a food processor if you have one. Process for 2-3 minutes. Mix in the eggs, then add the ground almonds and almond extract and blend until well combined.
Peel the apples, and cut thin slices of apple. Do this at the last minute to prevent the apple going brown. Arrange the slices over the biscuit base. Spread the frangipane filling evenly on top.
Level the surface and sprinkle with the flaked almonds.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden-brown and set.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool for 15 minutes. Remove the sides of the tin. An easy way to do this is to stand the tin on a can of beans and push down gently on the edges of the tin.
Transfer the tart, with the tin base attached, to a serving plate. Serve warm with cream, crème fraiche or ice cream.

title: Apple Pie
description: An Estonian sweet made with apple and buttermilk — serves 8, ready in under half an hour.

steps.text: Peel and clean apples/rhubarb, cut in to a slices.
Beat eggs and sugar together into a light foam.
Mix together flour, salt and baking powder.
Add the dry ingredients to the egg mixture and add sour milk gradually while stirring, Add berries.
Pour dough in to a butter greased pan. Sprinkle over sugar (and cinnamon). Bake at 180 C for 30 minute.

title: Apple pie pops
description: A Dominican sweet made with shortening, apple and cinnamon — makes 12, about an hour start to finish.

steps.text: Need Lollipop sticks Instructions for crust.
Combine the flour, sugar, and salt to a food processor bowl. Mix using the pulse setting.
Add butter and shortening and pulse about 10 -12 times until the texture is changed to small pebbles.
Add ¾ of the ice water and pulse a few more times until the dough takes the shape of a ball. Add more water as needed. Don't overmix. Don't worry if the dough isn't completely blended.
You will use your rolling pin to finish creating the crust.
Place dough ball onto the counter and flatten into a flat disc. Wrap it in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least an hour or overnight. Instructions for pie filling.
Heat butter over medium heat, until just golden brown.
Add brown sugar, spices, salt and lemon juice. Stir to combine ingredients Add diced apples and stir.
Allow apples to cook for about 5-7 minutes, over medium heat.
Remove from heat and let the apple mixture cool. You can place apples in the refrigerator to speed up the process. Mix egg and water for an egg wash.
Roll out pie dough to 1/8 inch thickness.
Cut out rounds of 2 ½ to 3 inches and place them on parchment paper. You will need to roll out the extra dough left over scraps from cutting.
In half of the rounds, cut out shapes or holes for ventilation purposes.
On the other half of the rounds, gently press one lollipop stick about halfway up each round.
Place one tablespoon of apple mixture in the center of each round.
Place each round on top of apples seal the edges.
Brush each pie pop with egg wash and sprinkle sugar on top.
Bake 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Apple Potato Mash (Hete bliksem)
description: A Dutch side of bacon, apple and potato — serves 4, on the table in about 45 minutes.

steps.text: Clean and peel the potatoes and cut them into even size chunks. Boil them in salted water for about 10 min and then add the cleaned and chopped apples into the boiling water. Add the cinnamon stick as well.
Leave to boil for another 10 minutes or until both apples and potatoes are to your liking. I like mine to be fairly chunky but that is a personal preference.
In the mean time bake the streaky bacon in a dry frying pan until crispy and set aside to drain on paper towels.
Slice a few apple pieces and melt a little butter in a fryin pan. Add the apple slices to it and add a bit of maple syrup into the pan as well as some cinnamon. Let it simmer until the apple is soft.
Prepare a plate with one whisked egg and one plate with sesame seeds. Cut your cheese into the required size. The smaller it is, the easier it is too handle.
Dip the cheese into the egg and make sure it coats all sides. Then dip the cheese into the sesame seeds and make sure it is covered everywhere.

Heat a non stick frying pan on high until nice and hot. Put the cheese slice in and bake until the sesame seeds are brown. You have to do this rather quickly or the cheese will melt completely. Turn and bake the other side.
Drain the apples and potatoes and mash them together. Taste and add cinnamon and salt where needed. Remove the cinnamon stick before mashing.

title: Apricot & Turkish delight mess
description: A Turkish sweet made with mascarpone, greek yoghurt and orange blossom water — serves 4, ready in under half an hour.

steps.text: Place the mascarpone, yogurt, sugar and orange flower water into a large bowl and whisk until thickened.
Fold the remaining ingredients through, then divide the mix between 2 dessert glasses or bowls and decorate with extra mint, if you like.

title: Arepa Pabellón
description: A Venezuelan dish of black beans, corn arepa filled with mozarella cheese and banana — serves 2, ready in under half an hour.

ingredients.name: corn arepa filled with mozarella cheese

steps.text: Prepare the meat in a skillet and add salt and pepper to taste, heat the beans over medium heat in a pan, fry or grill the ripe plantains as indicated on its package and cut the tomato into small cubes.
Reserve these ingredients until filling: preheat the grill or pan and grill the arepa, putting it once on each side until they are golden brown.
With the help of a knife, open it by the edge through the middle, creating a space to fill it with the ripe plantain, the beans, meat and chopped tomato.
Serve with a little pico de gallo or guacamole dip sauce.

title: Arepa pelua
description: A Venezuelan dish of beef, capsicum and cheese — serves 4, a slow cook that's worth the wait.

steps.text: Cook the meat: Place the flank steak in a pot with broth or water and salt. Cook over low heat for about 2 hours, until tender and easy to shred.
Shred the meat: Once cooked, drain and shred the meat using two forks.

Prepare the vegetables: Sauté chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic in a little oil. Add cumin, oregano, paprika, and salt. Stir in the meat and cook for a few minutes until the flavors are well combined.
Make the dough: In a bowl, mix the cornmeal with warm water and salt until a soft dough forms. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Form the arepas: Divide the dough into 6 portions, shape into balls, and flatten into thick discs.
Cook: Cook the arepas on a griddle or skillet over medium heat for 2–3 minutes on each side until golden. You can then bake them for a few minutes if you prefer them crispier.
Fill: Slice the arepas open on one side, fill with the hot shredded beef, and top with grated cheese.

title: Arnhemse meisjes
description: Thin, crisp Dutch cookies made from a folded sheet of puff pastry, cut into rounds and rolled out in sugar, then chilled and baked until caramelised.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: generous amount for the work surface and coating; amount not given

steps.text: Fold the puff pastry sheet over itself into three even layers, about 1 cm thick in total.
Cut as many 3 cm rounds as you can from the folded dough, placing the cutter close together because the trimmings can't really be reused.
Sprinkle sugar generously over the work surface. Put a dough round on it, sprinkle a little more sugar on top, and roll in one direction into an oval about 8 cm long, flipping it halfway.
Lay each oval on a baking tray lined with baking paper and repeat with the remaining rounds.
Chill the tray in the fridge for at least 30 minutes so the cookies hold their shape.
Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until golden and the sugar has caramelised. Watch them, because the sugar can burn quickly.
Move the cookies straight to a wire rack and let them cool completely; left on the tray, the sugar underneath overcooks.

title: Arra të Mbushura me Fik Walnut Stuffed Figs (with Fig Syrup)
description: An Albanian sweet made with figs and walnuts — serves 2, on the table in about 45 minutes.

steps.text: Prepare the Figs: cut off the hard bits of stalk and then cut the figs in half length ways.
Place the figs in a small frying pan / saute pan with the cut side face up and add the water around them. Cooking.
Leave the figs on a medium heat to cook through, once they become soft remove them from the pan and place onto a serving dish. This will take around 10 - 15 minutes. Prepare the Syrup.

In the pan there will be a red water juice left from the figs. Add the sugar while remaining on a medium heat. Stir continuously for a couple of minutes until the juice has turned to a thick syrup. Remove from the heat. Serving.
Push one half of walnut into every fig and then drizzle the syrup over the top. Serve warm or cooled.

title: Arroz al horno (baked rice)
description: Valencian oven-baked rice with pancetta, bacon and morcilla, cooked in a tomato, onion and pepper sofrito, topped with rosemary and finished with lemon and parsley.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: extra virgin, half for the meats and half for the sofrito

ingredients.name: bacon
ingredients.note: fine smoked bacon or lardons, diced

ingredients.name: black pudding
ingredients.note: morcilla sausages, whole or cut in 2.5 cm pieces

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: half a lemon's juice in the rice, the rest squeezed over to serve

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Heat half the olive oil in a large flat pan over medium-high heat and fry the pancetta until golden. Remove, let it cool, and cut it into 1.25 cm pieces.
In the same pan fry the large bacon lardons and diced bacon for 3 to 4 minutes, then set aside with the pancetta.
Fry the morcilla, whole or in 2.5 cm pieces, for 3 to 4 minutes and set it aside with the other cooked meat.
Scrape up the browned bits and lower the heat to medium. Add the rest of the oil and the onion and fry for 4 minutes until it begins to turn golden.
Add the garlic and red pepper and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the grated tomato and smoked paprika, season, and cook on medium for another 5 minutes until everything softens.
Add the rice and mix it through the sofrito. Add about half the cooked meat, half the stock and the juice of half a lemon, and level the rice into an even layer.
Turn the heat to high and slowly add the rest of the stock until everything is covered and bubbling. Arrange the remaining meat on top and cook for 5 to 6 minutes.
Take it off the heat, add the rosemary sprigs, and bake in the 180°C oven for 20 to 25 minutes (move it to an ovenproof dish first if the pan isn't ovenproof).
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon juice.

title: Arroz con gambas y calamar
description: Rice with squid and prawns: both seared first, then a sofrito of onion, red pepper and crushed tomato, rice and hot fish stock simmered together and rested covered.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a saucepan and sear the squid rings, then lift them onto a plate. Sear the prawns quickly in the same pan and set them aside too.
In the same oil, soften the onion, then add the finely chopped red capsicum and the crushed tomato and cook into a sofrito base.
Heat the stock in a separate pan. Turn up the heat under the sofrito, add the rice and fry it for about 2 minutes, until it changes colour.
Return the squid with its juices and stir. Pour in the hot stock, add a little salt and bring to the boil.
When the rice starts to bubble, reduce to medium heat and cook for 18 minutes, checking that the stock is spread evenly.
Turn off the heat; a little broth will remain. Cover the pot and leave it for 5 minutes, then serve with the seared prawns (the translated transcript doesn't say when they go back into the pot).

title: Arroz con Leche
description: A Colombian sweet made with rice, condensed milk and cinnamon stick — makes 10, worth the couple of hours it takes.

steps.text: In a small pot, add water and cinnamon sticks, bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes. Set aside and discard cinnamon sticks.
Place the rice and the cinnamon water in a large saucepan, over medium heat and cook for 5 minutes.
Add salt, butter, vanilla extract, 2 cups of milk, and sugar. Stir well to mix and cook uncovered for approximately 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium low. Add the remaining milk and condensed milk. Stir with a wooden spoon. Cook for 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until the rice pudding thickens to desire consistency.
Stir well and remove from heat, and let it cool at room temperature. The consistency should be very creamy. Refrigerate for a least 1 hour or overnight.

title: Asado
description: An Argentinian dish of chorizo, chuck steak and black pudding — makes 10, on the table in about 45 minutes.

steps.text: Prepare the Fire: Start a wood fire in your grill and let it burn down to coals.
Season the Meat: Generously salt the beef cuts.
Grill the Meat: Place the beef on the grill, starting with the thickest cuts farthest from the coals. Add chorizo and morcilla after the beef has been cooking for a while.
Cook to Perfection: Cook the meat, turning occasionally, until it reaches your desired doneness. Typically, ribs may take up to 2 hours; thinner cuts will cook faster.
Rest and Serve: Let the meat rest for about 10 minutes before slicing. Serve with chimichurri sauce and grilled vegetables.

title: Aubergine & hummus grills
description: A Turkish dish of aubergine, bread and hummus — serves 4, on the table in about 45 minutes.

steps.text: Lay the aubergine out in one layer on a large baking sheet. Brush sparingly with vegetable oil, then season generously. Grill for 15 mins, turning twice and brushing with oil until the slices are softened and cooked through.
Meanwhile, whizz the bread into crumbs. Add 2 tsp oil and whizz briefly again, to coat.

Spread a couple of tsps of hummus on top of each slice of aubergine. Tip the breadcrumbs onto a large plate, then press the hummus side of the aubergines into the crumbs to coat. Grill again, crumb-side up, for about 3 mins until golden.
Toss the walnuts, parsley and cherry tomatoes in a bowl, season, then add the lemon juice and olive oil and toss again. Serve the grills with the salad, a dollop more hummus and some pitta bread.

title: Aubergine couscous salad
description: A Turkish salad of goat's cheese, aubergine and couscous — serves 4, on the table in about 45 minutes.

steps.text: Heat grill to high. Put the aubergine on a baking sheet, brush with oil and season. Grill for about 15 mins, turning and brushing with more oil halfway, until browned and softened.
Meanwhile, tip the couscous into a large bowl, pour over the stock, then cover and leave for 10 mins. Mix the tomatoes, mint, goat’s cheese and remaining oil together.
Fluff the couscous up with a fork, then stir in the aubergines, tomato mixture and lemon juice.

title: Warm banana tapioca pudding (chè chuối chưng)
description: Small tapioca pearls simmered in coconut milk with pandan, sugar and sliced ripe bananas, served warm with toasted sesame seeds and peanuts.

ingredients.name: banana
ingredients.note: ripe, medium to large, about 454 g

ingredients.name: peanuts
ingredients.note: roasted, unsalted, roughly chopped, to garnish

steps.text: Toast the sesame seeds and set them aside.

Bring 1½ cups water to a boil in a medium saucepan, sprinkle in the tapioca pearls and stir. Partly cover, reduce to low and simmer for about 15 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until most pearls are soft and translucent.
Pour in the coconut milk, sugar and salt. Add the pandan leaves, tied in a knot or torn in half, raise the heat slightly and simmer a few minutes, stirring now and then, until the sugar dissolves.
Peel the bananas and slice them crosswise about 2.5 cm thick. Add to the pan and stir to coat in the coconut milk.
Simmer gently for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring carefully so the bananas don't turn mushy, until slightly softened.
Turn off the heat, cover, and leave for about 15 minutes so the pandan flavour infuses.
Serve warm, sprinkled with the toasted sesame seeds and chopped peanuts.

title: Authentic Norwegian Kransekake
description: Norwegian wreath cake: rings of ground almonds, icing sugar and egg white, chilled, rolled into ropes, baked in ring forms, piped with icing and stacked. Makes a tower of 18 rings.

ingredients.name: almonds
ingredients.note: ground in a grinder or processor, not almond flour

ingredients.name: egg whites
ingredients.note: 3 for the dough, 1 added slowly later

ingredients.name: semolina
ingredients.note: for dusting the greased forms, no amount given; flour or breadcrumbs also work

ingredients.name: egg whites
ingredients.note: for the icing; water (or cream, per the video) if avoiding raw egg

steps.text: Grind the almonds. Mix with the icing sugar, add three egg whites and knead into a ball. Wrap and chill for at least an hour, ideally overnight.
Grease the kransekake forms thoroughly and coat with semolina, flour or breadcrumbs.
Heat the oven to 210°C top and bottom heat. Divide the dough into six pieces.
Knead the remaining egg white into the dough little by little (dip your fingers in it if the dough is dry) and roll ropes about as thick as a finger.
Lay the ropes in the forms and pinch the ends together to make rings. Keep them on the thin side as they puff up.
Bake in the middle of the oven for 10-12 minutes until golden, in two rounds, watching closely so they do not burn.
Cool the rings. Mix the icing from icing sugar, egg white and lemon juice and pipe a zigzag on each ring, largest first.
Stack the rings into a tower, either gluing each with icing as you go or waiting for it to dry first.

title: Avocado dip with new potatoes
description: An Australian dish of avocado, yoghurt and lime — serves 4, about an hour start to finish.

steps.text: Whizz half the avocado flesh with the yogurt, lime and lemon juice and seasoning. Dice the remaining avocado, then gently stir into the whizzed mix with most of the lime zest. Cover, then chill until ready to serve.
Boil potatoes for 6 mins, then drain well and toss with olive oil, chilli powder and cumin seeds. Now set aside until half an hour before your guests arrive.
Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6, then roast potatoes for about 30 mins, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and tender.
Transfer the dip to one or two bowls, scatter with the remaining lime zest and serve with the hot potatoes, and tortilla chips for dipping.

title: Ayam Percik
description: Chicken marinated in a spiced onion, garlic and ginger paste, roasted, then coated in a coconut cream and chilli percik sauce and finished under the grill.

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: about 100 g, or about 5 shallots; for the marinade

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: about 100 g, or about 5 shallots; for the sauce base paste

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.note: about 1 inch; for the sauce base paste

ingredients.name: lemongrass
ingredients.note: stalks, inner white core; for the sauce base paste

ingredients.name: candlenuts
